claims.quote: Her fingers found the dented brass of the compass she still carried—so familiar it had grooves where her thumb had worn them.
A length of braided hair, knotted and wrapped until it looked more like rope than ornament, was looped around her wrist.
The deck smelled of hot tar and rope, of sweat and toasted cumin from the market stalls beyond the quay.

claims.quote: Gulls thinned the air like thrown coins.

claims.quote: "And you still count the ropes by twos," she answered. "You do it in the dark like my mother made you.
She trusts Amina's judgement but warns when lines are crossed.
Nasir lurked by the binnacle, the old oilcloth-wrapped ledger tucked under his arm, his fingers black at the nails from ink and tar.
A thin white scar ran along the knuckle of his right hand

She had once trimmed a mizzen in a sudden squall, cutting with a knife that had belonged to her father until the sail rode small and the spar stayed—there were rooms of the crew's memory where that night lived like a map.
"Hold the line, Mina," it said, and the voice was not spoken aloud, and it was the voice she loved and could not bring back.
They had been children once, hiding behind the same empty barrel in a different port, stealing olives and sharing the one sweet bite between them.
When the Simorgh swung at her moorings under the blistering sun of Port Rahim, Amina al-Sirafi stood at the rail
